version: V4 single additional whole-body filledness gate, authorized and frozen before runs
onlyClassifierChange: After V3's unchanged local filled-disk gate, require whole-body inkArea/hullArea >=0.82. inkArea is the cardinality of the unchanged unique thicknessPixels (residual offshaft pixels plus the same actual original black shaft pixels between existing attachment rows). Each pixel is a unit square. hullArea is the continuous shoelace area of the convex hull of ALL CORNERS of ALL these unit squares. No pixel-center lattice denominator, raster rounding, bounding-box area or filled-hole convention is substituted. A monotone-chain hull removes interior collinear corners deterministically.
constant: The0.82 filled-body value is fixed for this version, carried from the earlier filled-interior criterion and now applied to the complete measured footprint. This gate was proposed after the V3 source diagnosis, so p10/case176/half-scale examples are development evidence, not blinded validation. No tuning after V4 results.
witnesses: Add inkArea,hullArea,solidity fields to each accepted body. All old body bounds, disk, source footprint runs, original shaft-body pixels, attachment rows, explained paths and owners remain unchanged. The new gate can only reject V3 body proposals.
controls: Same case176; original36four-core; unchanged original29 plus attached addendum6; realpages23,28,29,38,39 and newp10 at their unchanged raster scales. Full case176 and absence of false p10/previous8spans required. Record remaining filled/hollow and3head misses openly. Root alone runs full39 if bounded controls support. No combined experiments until standalone39 clear.
integration: Only final expansion-only alternatives as V3. No source pixel edits or ordinary component changes. Exact previous candidate snapshots and source obligations retained. Production unchanged.
scope: Conservative filled-body recognition with explicit abstention. A high whole-body fill fraction is not a proof of musical note identity; compact filled glyphs and damaged notes remain possible ambiguities. No robust-recognition claim from this bounded experiment.
